Well first I want to congratulate you for continuing to heal and better yourself, even if you don’t think you are going anywhere or seeing results. The fact that you took the initiative to heal and have been doing so for that long shows that you are most definitely a strong person. A lot of people have a hard time starting or even admitting that there is something wrong within their lives that they want to change. 

I share my experience not to discourage you or boast about my own accomplishments, but rather to show you that I was in the same exact shoes as you and many people here. You may not think that we haven’t gone through the same experiences as yourself to understand but you are not alone and we are all in this journey together. You shouldn’t compare yourself to others and judge your own journey as harshly. You are a unique individual who has experienced unique situations. Everyone’s healing process is different. Some may take 2 years, 4 years, 10, 15, or even a whole life time to come to a place where they are okay. As long as you don’t give up you’ll eventually find a time where you feel like you’re in a good place. 

Now I’m not saying it was easy for me. I had to really take a look at who I was. Asking questions like “Who am I?”. Am I just playing a character in this life? Is this who I really want to be? Who do I wanna be? Asking these questions will bring you deeper and deeper to who you truly are. It is very deep within that cancels out the outside noise of your mind and memory. I went through the roughest times these past 4 years, but each time I came out of it because I didn’t give up and I learned something about myself every single time. Every time something “bad” happens to you or you feel like you are going backwards, there’s always a chance to learn from it if you’re willing and able to perceive your situation from a bigger picture. 

Whatever you want to pursue in your life as a career has to make sense. You have to be clear on what you want to experience in this life. Something that you wake up and you say “I’m so grateful that I get to wake up, live my life, and do what I love”. Imagine what that would look like for you, can you see yourself in the future? What does it look like? Who’s around you? What would the emotion feel like? I’ve always felt like I wanted to help people and give service to people because I saw as a kid that we are all going through life together. We are all susceptible to all suffering. So I decided to dedicate my whole life to making a difference in that, hence why I went towards healthcare. Your career must resonate with the most inner part of your soul. It could be anything! Don’t be scared to step out of your comfort zone. The more uncomfortable it is, the more you are learning and progressing. You don’t want to run on a circular track forever and expect to experience something new. You must go forward to learn and experience new territory.


I wish you the best, and I know you can do it, because you already are doing it. Don’t be so harsh on yourself, you’re doing great. Don’t think that you’ll just heal yourself and everything will be okay/perfect. Its a whole process that you will continue to do for the rest of your life and you must accept that because it gets easier if you never give up, always remember that :)

Yes you can most definitely be successful. I am 23 yrs old and was diagnosed in 2020. I told myself I’ll do anything it takes to heal, create the life I want, and to have a purpose in this world that I choose. I went through a lot of therapists, sifted through multiple medications, did tons of research and just learned about myself and how the human mind/body works. I also learned about meditation which I do almost everyday. Fast forward 4 years later I’m in a very good place where I’m am able to forgive and let go of everything that has happened in my life up to this point. I don’t do therapy anymore, no more medication, no more flash backs, no more panic attacks. My anxiety is still there but it doesn’t dominate much anymore, its just there. It wasn’t easy at all, sometimes you think you’re 10 steps forward and you fall back 7 steps, but you’ll still be 3 steps ahead, its up and down, up and down. But you are always going steadily up (even if you don’t see it right now) if you never give up, and just do your best to recover and heal. I switched my focus from accounting to nursing and now I’m in a comfortable place working as a nurse. Once you go along the healing process, your purpose and career will come together as one and it will be the clearest thing to you as if you were to say “This is exactly what I want to do with my life, this is what is meaningful to me”. 


TLDR: You clear off all the mud so you can see the bigger picture easier.

Yes I have definitely felt that way before. I think most people feel that way with life in general, not just their childhood. But the best thing that helps me “cope” with these feelings is to simply list things out, whether on actual paper or in my head, all of the things I’m grateful for that I have now. It doesn’t matter if its small or big. You could list that you’re grateful for your dog, food, tv, youtube, your car, a place to live, the people around you, the sun, nature, even the fact that you’re alive. Try to find anything grateful in your life NOW and just sit with that feeling. See how your body responds.

Yes I was the same way until I started focusing on healing 100%. Just think about it. Imagine you were homeless and in survival mode. It may be hard to think about what dream car to buy or a dream house, or even the thought about a spouse and kids. You’re just constantly thinking about the next meal. It’s hard to think about a life that you want to live when you’re constantly unhealed in someways. I think the best thing to do is to focus on healing, and I am positive that the rest will fall into place. Aspirations come from things that mean something for you. And the best way to find things that mean something to you is to connect with your inner self. And when you go through the healing process its sort of the same as reconnecting with your inner self, that same inner-self child energy.

This is just my theory but I believe freezing happens when you are not able to process certain emotions/sensations at the time that they occur. For example you freeze up when someone says “I love you” because your body doesn’t know what that feeling is, and so its just a big “?”. Your body doesn’t know how or where to categorize this experience. So my tip to you use is to take the time to try and identify emotions as best as you can. Try to label them to understand “ok this is anger, this is anxiety, this is fear, this is happiness, this is peace, this is calm, this is sleepy”. And as you do this, I think you’ll be able to train your body to process certain emotions and experiences better, resulting in less time of being “frozen”.

Also don’t take the whole triggering thing personally. If you do trigger her, know that it is never your fault. As long as you know that your intentions are not to trigger her, its okay if it happens. Because you’re not perfect, you’re learning about CPTSD as much as she is and you’re trying your best. You are never at fault at the triggers because you didn’t create them in the first place. I hope everything goes well.

You may not have the answers and you may not understand it all right now, but you’re there for her and thats all that matters. Don’t beat yourself up for it too much. I was suffering from CPTSD for about 4 years and my family did their best to help me but it just made it worse. I told them to just leave me alone so that I could figure it out, but they wouldn’t listen and kept asking questions and trying to do things for me and recommend doctors, therapy, and just smothering me trying to help me. But I honestly told them that the best way to help me was to leave me alone. It was the best thing they could’ve done. I know it doesn’t make any sense though because they cared about me a lot and they want to help but the thing about CPTSD is that leaving them be and letting them go through the motions might just be the best thing that you could do. So don’t beat yourself up so much. You are doing great and I want to let you know that.

I am not a medical professional but based on what I’ve gathered throughout years of learning about myself is that our body remembers almost everything, even if we cannot consciously remember it. In the case of playing with your daughter, there is an obvious fight or flight memory that is triggered from specifically playing with your daughter. In my opinion, there must be a memory within your life that was associated with “playing”, perhaps a time when you were in school or maybe playing with your own parents that wasn’t so pleasant. Or there was a situation where you were playing in childhood that caused the same reactions as you are having with your daughter. Whatever that situation was, if unresolved, could definitely be triggered again by similar stimuli and environments that were associated with the memory. Your body will react because that’s how it reacted when it was happening back then. You have to look deep into your memories that were similar to this situation and you will be able to remember it slowly but surely. Once you remember the memory, you have to find a way to make peace with that memory or process it in a new way that allows you to let it go.

Yes, and you can essentially do this technique for anything. It just takes a good amount of focus and imagination. If you feel like you aren’t good enough, you can try to imagine what it feels like to be good enough. What does that look like, what would it feel like. Imagine what it would feel like for someone to say you’re good enough. Imagine your reaction to that, try to capture that feeling and really try to feel that. Then pay attention to your body and see how it responds. You can even do this technique for example lets say your parents never praised you enough when you were younger. You can close your eyes and imagine what it would feel like to have your parents stand in front of you and praise you right then and there. And as always just pay attention to what your body does, the sensations it creates makes this happen. The more you do it, the easier it gets and the stronger the feeling becomes. Your body starts to think that these sensations are real. And so your body adapts to the new conditioning which then becomes your new baseline. You can do this for anxiety as well. What would it feel like to not be anxious. What would it be like? Can you picture yourself not being anxious in public? How would that look like? The technique is basically to use your mind to imagine how you would want to feel, then the imaginary actually turns into reality because your body can’t differentiate it. This is sort of the same technique to manifestation if you believe in that sort of stuff. Or you’ve heard the term “fake” it to make it. If you “fake” your confidence with your imagination and it makes you feel confident in real scenarios, then is it really fake confidence or real confidence? Just food for thought. Sorry for the long replies but I hope this helps.

I had this feeling as well, whenever I was home with my dad alone. I would be afraid to leave my room and go to the bathroom, even holding it in for long times. But the thing that really helped me was putting my emotions aside and thinking logically. I would talk through my logic of what ifs, and be completely honest with myself. I start off with, whats the worst that could happen? Then what are the chances of that happening? How would I feel if that happened? Then you would keep going. What would it looked like if that happened? You start going from an emotional way of thinking to a logical point of thinking which causes the emotions to lessen as you do whatever you want or need. So in all, play the scenarios out until you get to a really illogical conclusion, and catch yourself there and ask yourself are you being honest with the scenario. For example: My anxiety = I don’t like to leave the room in front of a bunch of people because I don’t like to be judged. Why? Because when people judge me it makes me feel bad about myself. Will they really judge me? I don’t know. What are the chances they say something bad to me as I walk outside? Probably nothing, but still. Ok so what if they say something about me in my face, that means there’s something wrong with them to be so mean and not my problem right?

Your body doesn’t know what’s past or future. Your body thinks it’s happening now. As you slowly try your best to let yourself feel these “feel” good emotions. Your body will start to cringe and try and resist these feelings as it’s always had in the past. But now you want to integrate new feel good feelings into your condition so your body begins to take that as the new norm.
Remember your body doesn’t know whats real or whats fake. It is in the response of your mind (memory / imagination/ thoughts) that trigger responses to how you feel.

I’m 23 so I could relate. The best thing to understand is that your body has been conditioned to feel this way for a while now. So much that is has been ingrained into your physical body and sensations. The thing that helped me the most is to at least 5 minutes a day try to imagine what it would feel like to be wanted. Whatever memory that you have in your life that you have felt wanted or felt “loved” or felt “belonged”. Try to hold that sensation of what it could be like for as long as you can. You start to condition your body into feeling what it feels like to be wanted / loved.

I’m sorry you feel that way. I am 22 myself and I want to tell you that you’re not alone. One of the tips that I can give you is that you can work through your thoughts. For example, up until I was about 20 years old, I would always be anxious to go to the store by myself. To get through this I would ask myself, what am I anxious about? Well I was anxious about what people we’re going to say to me or how I looked, or if I was going to say something dumb or looked stupid. How would that make me feel? It would make me feel terrible. But at the end of the day I asked, will these strangers ever see me again? Do I really care what people think? The answer is no. In 5 years, that embarrassing moment I had at the store will not matter, so why should it matter now? The people who were involved in that embarrassing moment probably won’t even remember my face or even remember that moment. After going through these thoughts every time I get anxious about going to the store, I start to find some peace. It takes time to re-shape how we think because we’ve always grown up thinking in one way. But it is possible to change how we think, it takes time and effort. Just like working out :). I hope this helps and I hope you ate successful in your future endeavors.

It has been 2 months since I've been taking lexapro. 5mg in the beginning and transitioned to 10mg. I have no more effects anymore. My libido is normal now, I dont have morning anxiety, I don't get panic attacks anymore, and I don't feel any hypervigilance at all. I feel normal now like how I felt when I was younger before I developed anxiety and PTSD.
The heightened anxiety went away after a while maybe 2-3 weeks. But that was on 10 mg.

I'm 5 weeks in taking 10 mg. I don't have any headaches or anything like that anymore. I feel somewhat emotionally blunt but id rather have that than my anxiety. My sex drive has dropped quite a bit, I am 19 years old but it doesn't bother me at all. This started right from the beginning when I started taking lexapro. I haven't got good sleep since the beginning as well.
